question_bank.stem: Occlusion sensitivity diagnoses a dog classifier by scanning what intervention over the image?

options.text: A dark square that partially masks regions of the input
A new label that replaces the dog class name
A learning-rate schedule applied to the optimizer
A pooled feature vector replacing the image

question_bank.rationale: The lecture describes placing a dark square over positions in the image and tracking how the dog score changes.

distractor_rationales.B: Changing the label name is not an input-region perturbation.
distractor_rationales.C: Optimizer schedules are training telemetry, not occlusion sensitivity.
distractor_rationales.D: A pooled feature vector relates to CAM, not the occlusion intervention.

source_ref.evidence_span: put the dark square on the top left of the image

frame_evidence.description: Slide shows a dark square scanning over a dog image while tracking how the dog score changes.

question_bank.stem: When the occluding square covers the dog face and the dog score drops, what does that support?

options.text: The model relies on the dog-face region for the class decision
The model ignores the dog-face region for the class decision
The model has switched to using benchmark contamination
The model has replaced the CNN head with a language model

question_bank.rationale: If covering the dog face changes the dog score, the masked face region is contributing to the decision.

distractor_rationales.B: A score drop is evidence the region matters, not that it is ignored.
distractor_rationales.C: Benchmark contamination is unrelated to an image occlusion test.
distractor_rationales.D: The experiment does not change the model into a language model.

source_ref.evidence_span: the square is partially occluding the face of the dog

frame_evidence.description: Slide examples include occlusion on the dog face, car wheel, and Afghan-hound image.

question_bank.stem: In the Afghan-hound example, occluding the human face increased the hound score. What diagnosis fits that behavior?

options.text: The human face was distracting evidence for the classifier
The human face was the main positive evidence for the hound
The dark square erased the model weights permanently
The input image was converted into a feature-map average

question_bank.rationale: The instructor says occluding the human face removed unnecessary information, making the true class score higher.

distractor_rationales.B: If removing it raises the hound score, it was not positive hound evidence.
distractor_rationales.C: Occlusion changes the input image, not the stored model weights.
distractor_rationales.D: Feature-map averaging belongs to CAM construction, not this diagnosis.

frame_evidence.description: Slide examples include occlusion on the dog face, car wheel, and Afghan-hound image.

question_bank.stem: For class activation maps, why does replacing several fully connected layers with global average pooling help localization?

options.text: It preserves a traceable link between feature maps and class scores
It removes all convolutional feature maps before scoring
It forces the classifier to use post-softmax saliency
It makes the network train without any class labels

question_bank.rationale: The lecture explains that global average pooling assigns one number to each feature map without losing the link back to localized information.

distractor_rationales.B: CAM depends on the last convolutional feature maps, not removing them.
distractor_rationales.C: CAM uses class-specific weights, not post-softmax saliency.
distractor_rationales.D: The classifier still trains with class labels.

source_ref.evidence_span: Because we actually did not lose the localized information.

frame_evidence.description: Slide shows a CNN head modified with global average pooling before the final classifier.

question_bank.stem: A class activation map for the dog score is produced by combining which class-specific ingredients?

options.text: Feature maps weighted by the final classifier weights for dog
Raw pixels sorted by their grayscale values for dog
Training examples ranked by their file names for dog
Token embeddings averaged across the sentence for dog

question_bank.rationale: The lecture describes weighing feature maps with the weights from the final fully connected layer to create the class-specific map.

distractor_rationales.B: CAM combines feature maps, not sorted raw pixel intensities.
distractor_rationales.C: File names do not determine the activation heatmap.
distractor_rationales.D: Token embeddings are a transformer diagnostic, not a CNN CAM ingredient.

source_ref.evidence_span: weighing them with the weights of the last fully
